# Snyk Code test-variant rule allowlist
#
# This file is the canonical registry of Snyk Code rule IDs whose findings
# are analysed but NOT ingested into the code-scanning dashboard. Snyk
# reports a distinct `<rule>/test` rule ID when the finding sits in test
# code; entries here name those IDs exactly.
#
# What this does NOT do: it does not exclude any file from the scan. Snyk
# Code still analyses every test file, so a taint trace that runs from a
# test helper into production code is still found and still reported,
# under the ordinary (non-`/test`) rule ID that is never listed here.
# Filtering by rule ID rather than by path is what preserves that.
#
# Adding an entry: review every current finding for the rule first and
# confirm none of them is a defect worth fixing, then include the
# reviewer justification in the PR description. A `/test` rule ID that
# appears in a scan without being listed here fails the job, so the list
# can only widen deliberately.
#
# Each non-comment line is one exact Snyk Code rule ID.

# Test files seed and clear `document.cookie` in a jsdom document to set
# up read-path fixtures. These are fixture writes in a synthetic
# document, not cookie-setting code that ships. Both production writers
# (frontend/src/lib/theme/cookie.ts writeThemeCookie and
# frontend/src/pages/library/view-cookie.ts writeViewCookie) set Secure,
# neither is flagged by this rule, and both have tests asserting the
# attribute so the guarantee survives this entry.
javascript/WebCookieSecureDisabledByDefault/test

# Literal password strings in frontend API tests are request-body
# payloads asserted against a mocked fetch ("a strong password",
# "correct-horse-battery-staple"). They authenticate nothing. Real
# committed credentials are the job of gitleaks (every PR and push) and
# the TruffleHog history sweep, neither of which treats test files
# differently; this rule is a code-smell heuristic, not that control.
javascript/NoHardcodedPasswords/test
